extra.message: Jelleo SOL-011: `#[account(close = ...)]`. Verify (1) account is fully drained before close, (2) lamports go to a controlled destination, (3) any token accounts are closed via Token program, not just zeroed. See: github.com/Copenhagen0x/solana-security-standard#sol-011.

sss-exclusions: the account is fully drained (lamports AND any token balances) before close and its data is zeroed, AND it holds no delegated authority over other on-chain resources (mints, PDAs, vaults) that must be explicitly revoked before close
the close destination is program-controlled or a signer-validated key, not an attacker-supplied account
metadata.note: RE2-safe port: the scanner's depth-2 paren-balanced regex is rejected by Semgrep as "too large" (RE2 expands the nested {0,N} repetitions). This delimiter-bounded window flags `close =` within a 400-char #[account( ... ) region. It stops the window at ; { } and # — none appear inside an attribute, and stopping at # means the NEAREST #[account( wins so the finding lands on the right attribute even when two are adjacent. It favors recall over the scanner's exact paren-balancing; both flag the same real #[account(close = ...)] attributes incl. long multi-line ones. Known limit: a raw-string literal (r#"..."#) inside a constraint before close= would stop the window early — a theoretical Semgrep-only miss; the scanner still catches it.

extra.message: Jelleo SOL-006: raw `AccountInfo` (no Signer<>/Account<> type). If this account is a privileged CALLER, verify `account.is_signer == true` before mutating state, or use Anchor's `Signer<>`. (A documented `/// CHECK:` account used only as a CPI target / program ID / read-only ref is fine — this is a heuristic flag.) See: github.com/Copenhagen0x/solana-security-standard#sol-006.

sss-exclusions: the AccountInfo is a documented `/// CHECK:` used only as a CPI target, program id, or read-only/sysvar ref — not a privileged caller whose signature matters
account.is_signer is asserted (or the field is a Signer<>/Account<>) before any state mutation
the account is never used to authorize a state change or fund movement — on-chain OR by an off-chain consumer of its emitted/logged key
